submission.bindingBasis: Planning anticipated checkpoint beta as complete at revision 3 (checkpointDigest sha256:797f...), but consequenceBoundaryEvidence reports the owner changed and the Task revision advanced after planning. The owner contract requires expectedRevision matching; stale expectedRevision fails REVISION_CONFLICT/not_committed. Since the revision has advanced, I cannot know whether the updated Task state still supports the beta-as-complete semantic transition without observing the current state and revision.
submission.rationale: The owner action contract makes checkpoint success contingent on matching the expectedRevision. ConsequenceBoundaryEvidence confirms the Task revision advanced after planning (ownerChanged=true). Acting with the stale planning binding would predictably fail REVISION_CONFLICT/not_committed. The contract notes that "after resume a semantically still-applicable checkpoint may be rebased onto the current revision," which requires observing the current revision and state first. I should not infer semantic applicability from planning-time evidence alone once the owner changed. Reobserving is required to determine whether a rebase is warranted, whether the consequence is no longer applicable, or whether to hold.
